concepts.def: Town vocabulary: el ayuntamiento (town hall), la plaza, el centro comercial, las afueras (outskirts), el barrio (neighbourhood).
Giving directions: sigue todo recto (carry straight on), gira a la derecha/izquierda (turn right/left), cruza la plaza.
Weather uses hacer and hay: hace sol, hace frío, hace calor, llueve (it rains), nieva (it snows), hay niebla (it is foggy).
Environment vocabulary: la contaminación (pollution), reciclar, la basura, proteger la naturaleza, ahorrar agua y energía.
Use hay for 'there is/are' ('Hay un parque') and está/están to locate specific places ('El museo está en el centro').
Getting around: en coche, en autobús, en tren, en bicicleta, a pie (on foot), and la estación for catching transport.

walkthroughs.body_html:
Area C: The World Around Us — a core area of GCSE Spanish.

Working through it builds the schema you need: the key terms, how they connect, and how to use them together.

Area C: The World Around Us brings together several ideas you need to use as a set, not in isolation.

Lock in the vocabulary first, then practise pulling the ideas together to answer real questions.

Use the activities in this adventure to build familiarity with Area C: The World Around Us.

Practise vocabulary, calculations and free-text questions to lock in the learning.

mcqs.q: 'Gira a la derecha' tells you to do what?
options: Turn right
Turn left
Go straight on
Stop
It is hot
It is cold
It is raining
It is windy

mcqs.q: How do you say 'there is a park in my town'?
options: Hay un parque en mi ciudad
Está un parque en mi ciudad
Es un parque en mi ciudad
Tiene un parque mi ciudad es
Pollution
Recycling
The countryside
A traffic jam

mcqs.q: How do you say 'it is hot' when talking about the weather?
options: 'Hace calor' - weather expressions use the verb hacer.
'Tiene calor el cielo.'
'Es caliente', translating the English 'is' directly.
Está is only used for people, never places.

mcqs.q: Can 'hay' and 'está' be used interchangeably for places?
options: Active.
No - hay introduces the existence of something ('Hay un cine'), while está locates a specific known place ('El cine está cerca').
Hay and está both just mean 'is', so either works.
Está is only used for people, never places.

mcqs.q: What does 'actual' mean in Spanish, as in 'el problema actual'?
options: Está is only used for people, never places.
Actual or real, as in English.
Active.
Current or present-day - 'the current problem'.
